title: Old Kentucky Minstrels: management and South Carolina towns
summary: One man was manager and boss; the show played mostly South Carolina, and the band began to play more modern, swinging material.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I see. Who was in charge of the Old Kentucky Minstrels? I mean, who coordinated where they were going to play the next? Was there a manager?
No. Just the manager and the boss were all the same. He'd take care of everything.
I see. The Old Kentucky Minstrels, though, traveled into South Carolina.
Yeah, mostly South Carolina. A.G. Allen was mostly in North Carolina.
What were some of the towns in South Carolina that they'd play? Like Spartanburg...?
Orangeburg... There are so many of them down there...
Do you recall at that time hearing much other music in Charleston or any of the other cities in South Carolina that were similar to what you were doing, what the bands...what you had been doing...?
Well, during that time, a little bit later... Later the (?) started. The Old Kentucky Minstrels started to play a little bit more modern stuff, and swing more. There was more outlets(?), you know.
Oh, I see. How many musicians were with the Old Kentucky troupe?
